assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson closed the Standard Model and is a clue found in nature, not an elegant idea left unconfirmed. The 2013 prize recognised the theory; the measurement of the particle itself, two independent detectors and a decade of coupling measurements, is arguably the largest unrecognised discovery in the field and has clear existential weight for how we understand mass.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over thousands of people and two collaborations. Gianotti (ATLAS spokesperson at the time), Jenni (ATLAS founding spokesperson) and Virdee (CMS founder and former deputy spokesperson) give one workable three-person configuration across both experiments. Della Negra, also a CMS founder, would be excluded and that is a genuine cost. The Nobel statutes' limit of three makes this structurally awkward.
assessment.maturity: Discovery in 2012 with independent confirmation in both experiments and extensive follow-up on spin, parity and couplings. The interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: The fair allocation among ATLAS and CMS founders is unresolved and any three-name set omits important figures.
The committee may judge that the collaboration-wide nature of the work makes individual attribution unsatisfying.
Details of who led which analysis and who proposed which detector design are from memory and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy by detecting a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, with the TXS 0506+056 blazar association and later evidence from the Galactic plane and NGC 1068. It is a new window on the universe built on an extraordinary instrument, and it ties directly to the origin of cosmic rays. This is a discovery that nature supplied, rather than an unconfirmed theory.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the clear scientific driver and long-time principal investigator. Karle and Spiering were central to the construction, analysis and collaboration leadership. The credit is plausible but not unique, since AMANDA, Baikal and ANTARES pioneers could also be argued for, and the collaboration is large.
assessment.maturity: The 2013 evidence and 2018 to 2023 follow-ups are strong, but individual source identification is still evolving and independent confirmation by KM3NeT is still developing. The core detection of a diffuse flux is well established.
uncertainties: The relative roles of Halzen, Karle, Spiering and others in the decisive detection are not fully settled from the supplied text.
Source-level associations are still being refined, so the prize may be seen as slightly early for the astrophysical interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators created a new class of quantum matter with protected edge and surface states. The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect, its observation in HgTe quantum wells and the experimental discovery of three-dimensional topological insulators form a clear chain from idea to nature. It is a major and conceptually clean discovery that follows the 2016 topological-phase prize while being distinct from it.
assessment.attribution: Kane is the theoretical anchor, Molenkamp led the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state, and Hasan the first experimental three-dimensional topological insulator work. Mele (co-author of the Kane-Mele proposal) would be left out, as would Bernevig, Zhang and others with a possible claim. The configuration is defensible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of independent confirmation across many materials and platforms; the interpretation is stable. The timing is mature.
uncertainties: Whether Mele must accompany Kane is an unresolved allocation question.
Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe proposal, which is not among the credited names, may be considered decisive for the experimental realisation.
The 2016 Nobel prize may make the committee reluctant to return to topological matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of flat bands at the magic angle and the 2018 discovery of correlated insulator and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire materials field, a platform where strong correlations can be tuned in a lab. It is original, clear and has produced a huge amount of follow-up work.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key prediction of the magic angle in 2011, and Jarillo-Herrero led the experimental discovery. This is a clean theory plus experiment pairing, which fits the three-person structure well, though Cory Dean and others working on related moire systems could be argued for in a wider framing.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is only about eight years old, though many groups confirmed it. Open questions about the pairing mechanism remain, and the field is still developing rapidly, so the long-term stable interpretation is not yet settled.
uncertainties: The superconducting mechanism is still debated, so the maturity of the interpretation is partial.
Possible premature recognition relative to other candidates with longer track records.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP's all-sky maps and parameter fits turned cosmology into a precision science, fixing the age, composition and geometry of the universe and giving strong support for a nearly scale-invariant primordial spectrum. It is a flagship observational result tied to my own field of cosmology, and it provides the clues from nature that theories of dark energy and inflation have to answer to.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was a principal instrument scientist and Spergel provided the central cosmological analysis. This is a reasonable three-person set, but WMAP was a large team effort and its science partially overlaps with COBE (2006) and Planck, which would raise priority and overlap questions.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently confirmed by Planck. The 2006 and 2019 prizes have already covered part of this territory, so a further prize may be judged a repetition rather than a new discovery.
uncertainties: The overlap with the COBE prize and the 2019 cosmology prize could count against it.
Planck's role and the credit of other WMAP team members are not covered by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and provide a new tool for tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and dark-matter searches. The idea of the magic wavelength lattice is original and it has been fully realised in experiment.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and Ye demonstrated the leading performance and applications. The credit pairing is strong and clear. The optical-clock part of the 2005 prize has been recognised before for the frequency comb, so the committee would need to see this as a distinct advance.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in many labs worldwide, and a redefinition of the second is under discussion. This is mature, though the main practical impact is still to come.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the work as an extension of the 2005 and 2012 prizes rather than a new discovery.
The roles of ion-clock groups such as NIST Al+ or Yb+ work are outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2023 evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, seen as correlated timing residuals across pulsars, opens a new gravitational-wave band that complements LIGO. It is a nature-supplied clue that connects to supermassive black holes, and possibly to new physics, which is attractive from a gravity theorist's perspective.
assessment.attribution: Several PTA collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, IPTA) found independent evidence, and the credit is difficult to allocate. McLaughlin and Siemens are NANOGrav leaders, and Kramer leads the European effort. This captures a plausible international trio but not the entire work, with notable others such as Hellings and Downs, or Detweiler, omitted.
assessment.maturity: The evidence is at about 3 to 4 sigma and the origin (supermassive black-hole binaries versus cosmological sources) is not established. This is premature for a prize and I would want to see a more definitive detection.
uncertainties: The statistical significance does not yet reach a discovery threshold.
Credit across multiple PTA collaborations is hard to resolve.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of the Hubbard model with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition to fermionic Mott states and quantum gas microscopes, gave a controllable laboratory for strongly correlated many-body problems. It has deep impact across condensed matter and quantum information, though its payoff on real materials questions is still partial.
assessment.attribution: Greiner (and Bloch) demonstrated the Mott insulator, Esslinger the fermionic Mott state, and the theory by Jaksch, Zoller and Cirac proposed the scheme. The theory would not fit within the three names if the experimental trio is chosen, and the experimental trio omits Cirac and Zoller. That tradeoff is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: The experimental techniques are well confirmed in many labs. The simulation of problems that classical computers cannot solve is still developing.
uncertainties: Theory versus experiment credit allocation is unresolved, and Zoller and Cirac may merit consideration through a separate candidate.
Overlap with the 2001 and 2012 prizes on cold atoms.
